headline: Canada Eases Chinese Steel Tariffs After U.S. Warned of a Trade Backdoor
facebook_description: Canada is extending tariff relief for Chinese metals through 2028, adding 23 steel and nine aluminum tariff items. In return, China will suspend tariffs affecting about C$400 million in Canadian pork and seafood exports. The agreement follows failed U.S.–Canada trade negotiations in August, when steel tariff relief and trade policy alignment were at issue. A $19 million U.S. customs settlement announced in May illustrates the longstanding enforcement concern; it does not establish wrongdoing under the new agreement. Who benefits as Ottawa diversifies its trade? Follow EP News for evidence-led reporting. #Canada #China #Steel #Trade
